summary: The sealed artifact has a credible retained Nord Stage 4 surface, passing package gates, and a sizable serialized Stage 3 state/probe model for programs, organ, synth, splits, scenes, morphs, and effects. It falls well short of the complete system contract: Grand/Upright/Electric are explicitly generated approximations rather than the required recorded sample sets; live browser key/MIDI playback still uses only the piano engine; organ and synth are represented by deterministic probes instead of being mixed into the actual Web Audio note path; Store As naming lacks a panel UI; many hardware bindings are state-only or shallow; and the runtime displays non-finite synth RMS.

criteria.label: Reference and regression retention
evidence: The desktop and narrow sealed captures show the complete red chassis, six ordered sections, two OLED locations, drawbar bank, effects controls, and 73-key keybed; evidence/stage3-capture.json reports no console messages or page errors for both 1440x900 and 390x844 captures.
src/App.test.tsx verifies 73 keys, E1-to-E7 range, 43 white/30 black keys, section order, section width fractions, and Program/Synth as the only primary OLEDs.
The narrow capture preserves the whole instrument but control labels are extremely small, so retention is inspectable rather than comfortably usable.

criteria.label: Complete hardware state fidelity
evidence: Interactive preview changes Program and Synth OLED text for page/program/live/split/scene/synth source actions, e.g. after clicks the Program OLED read LIVE 1 / Scene II / Split C3-C4-C5 and Synth read Super Saw / Arp Run.

src/App.tsx marks nearly all Organ/Program/Synth controls functional via functionalControlIds, with Aftertouch and Delay Tempo excluded, but many bindings are shallow state updates or status messages rather than canonical hardware behavior.
Drawbar LED ladders are rendered from a fixed index value in SectionView, not from the actual drawbar state, weakening hardware state fidelity.

criteria.label: Programs and Live Mode
evidence: stage3System.ts creates 32 program slots and 8 live slots, supports selectProgram, selectLiveSlot, storeProgram, storeAsProgram, dirty state, page buttons, program buttons, and program-dial listView state.
src/App.test.tsx exercises round-trip, Store/Store As helper path, Live auto-store, edit discard, page/program buttons, and dial navigation.

The artifact's own visual audit states Store As naming is only covered through the deterministic storeAsProgram API path rather than a text-entry modal or panel workflow; numeric list view is a boolean state, not a visible browsable list.

criteria.label: Layers, splits, scenes, and morphs
evidence: stage3System.ts models the documented 11 split positions and Off/6/12 crossfade values, scenes I/II, Wheel and Control Pedal morph assignment arrays, clock data, transpose, and Panic.
Panel Split only toggles a fixed C3/C4/C5 configuration; there is no visible editing of the 11 split positions or crossfade widths from the panel.

Morph assignment is hardcoded to synth.A.filter.cutoff and organ.A.level, with panel buttons clearing assignments rather than assigning arbitrary targets; master clock has serialized BPM/sync targets but no real tap/dial workflow in the UI.

criteria.label: Complete Organ system
evidence: stage3System.ts implements two organ layers, B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe harmonic tables, drawbar/register behavior, percussion, key click, vibrato/chorus, and rotary slow/fast/stop in renderOrganProbe; tests verify model and drawbar spectral differences.
Panel controls primarily alter layer A model/drawbars/percussion/vibrato/rotary; there is limited panel support for layer B focus/zones and no live organ note lifecycle through the keybed.
The visual audit explicitly says Organ/Synth live browser key playback is represented through state and deterministic render probes while the live Web Audio oscillator path remains piano-focused.

criteria.label: Complete Synth system
evidence: stage3System.ts defines three synth layers, Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H waveform lists, oscillator control, LP12/LP24/HP/BP filtering, envelopes, LFO waveforms, voice modes, and arpeggiatorSteps; tests render distinct probe outputs for these.

The UI exposes only a subset of canonical Synth editing: source buttons map Sample to Pure, Analog to Super, Wavetable to Multi, with Osc Select cycling all waves; voice priority, glide, hold, arp direction/range, LFO destination/sync, and independent layer routing are not fully panel-editable.
Runtime status in the sealed capture and my interactive pass displayed synth RMS as Infinity, indicating a non-finite synth probe/load issue despite tests sanitizing non-finite samples.

criteria.label: Distinct engine behavior
evidence: Tests compare deterministic Float32Array probes for organ models and synth waveforms/filters/envelopes/LFO/voice/arp and require non-zero distances, so there is some distinct generated behavior.
These are generated probe algorithms, not full live engine implementations; organ and synth are not connected to the actual browser key/MIDI playback path.
The non-finite synth RMS shown at runtime makes the quality and stability of the synth engine suspect even where tests pass.

criteria.label: Inherited graph and effects integration
evidence: createPianoEngine builds the real Web Audio graph for piano only; App.startKey and MIDI handlers call engineRef.current.noteOn/noteOff, which route into the piano engine.
Organ and Synth integration is represented by integrationSnapshot and render probes, not by actual Web Audio buses feeding the inherited effects/master destination.
Effects focus buttons for Organ/Synth only set a status message saying they are routed through the shared graph; no code connects organ/synth audio to that graph.

criteria.label: Musical quality, latency, and load
evidence: The artifact passes test/typecheck/lint/build and capture logs report no console/page errors.
Live play quality is limited to the inherited piano oscillator/sample-style engine; organ/synth are not audible from the keybed.
Status displayed 'Audio: piano + organ 0.125 + synth Infinity' in both sealed desktop evidence and interactive runtime, which is a visible runtime quality defect.

criteria.label: Canonical state round-trip
evidence: ProgramSnapshot serializes piano layers/performance, effects, organ, synth, split, scenes, morphs, clock, and transpose; store/load clones this state across 32 slots and Live slots.
Tests verify selected organ/synth/split edits survive Store As and program selection, and dirty edits are discarded on program change.
Round-trip evidence is mostly helper-level state testing; Store As naming is not exposed in the UI, and live audio/effect routing state is not validated against actual played organ/synth audio.

criteria.label: Required hardware bindings
evidence: All non-excluded controls have accessible labels and many have data-control-id values, but canonical behavior is uneven.

Several required workflows are shallow or missing: Store As has no text-entry UI, split point/crossfade editing is not panel-editable, morph assignment is hardcoded/clear-only, master clock tap/dial is not implemented, and organ/synth effect focus is status-only.

Excluded controls are honestly declared: program.morph-aftertouch and effects.delay-tempo are decorative, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json lists Extern, Aux KB, MIDI-out, aftertouch, preset libraries, pattern editing, and related exclusions.

criteria.label: Cross-system workflows
evidence: Interactive clicks update Program/Synth OLEDs and selected button states across Live, Split, Scene II, Vox, Super Saw, and Arp Run.

The cross-system workflow is primarily serialized state plus probe readouts; playing keys after changing organ/synth/splits still uses App.startKey -> pianoEngine.noteOn, so zones, scenes, morphs, organ, synth, and effects do not operate as one audible instrument.
Panic is triggered by a special double Transpose click condition rather than a dedicated canonical Panic control.

criteria.label: Inherited regression reliability
evidence: Local gates passed: pnpm test reported 18 passed tests, and typecheck, lint, and build all exited successfully.
The feature matrix retains Phase 1 and Phase 2 IDs including regression.phase1 and regression.phase2 mapped to src/App.test.tsx.

Phase 2 hard-gate regression is material: sampleLibrary and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json explicitly state Grand/Upright/Electric are generated approximations, not required bundled recorded sample sets.

criteria.label: System architecture
evidence: The code has separable hardware data, pianoEngine, and stage3System modules with normalized ProgramSnapshot state and cloning for serialization.
The architecture splits real Web Audio playback from Stage 3 deterministic probes, so organ/synth/effects integration is declarative rather than an actual unified engine path.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json claims one shared system model but also admits organ/synth live browser playback remains piano-focused in the visual audit.

criteria.label: Tests and maintainability
evidence: The feature matrix maps every required Stage 1-3 feature ID to a real test file, and the single test suite covers visual inventory, piano, effects, programs, organ, synth, and integration helpers.
Tests are concentrated in one large App.test.tsx and often exercise helper functions/render probes rather than the actual browser UI and real audio graph.
The inherited piano library test asserts generated-not-recorded provenance, which directly conflicts with the Phase 2/3 hard gate requiring recorded Grand/Upright/Electric sample sets.

criteria.label: Runtime performance
evidence: The production preview loaded and an interaction pass through Program, Live, Split, Scene, Organ, Synth, and Arp controls produced no browser console errors.
Repeated interactions visibly changed OLED/status state without crashing, and package build output was small.
Runtime quality is reduced by the visible synth Infinity readout and by the fact that organ/synth playback is not connected to the live key path.

issues.summary: Required recorded Grand/Upright/Electric sample sets are absent.
issues.evidence: src/pianoEngine.ts sampleLibrary and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json explicitly declare generated approximations/not recordings; the visual audit lists this as a known deviation.

issues.summary: Organ and Synth are not live keybed/MIDI audio engines.
issues.evidence: App.startKey and MIDI note handlers call pianoEngine.noteOn only; visual audit states Organ/Synth live browser key playback is represented by state/probes while the live Web Audio path remains piano-focused.

issues.summary: Organ/Synth/effects shared-routing integration is mostly declarative.
issues.evidence: integrationSnapshot declares a shared path, but the actual Web Audio graph is built in createPianoEngine for piano layer buses; Organ/Synth focus buttons only update status text.

issues.summary: Program and performance workflows are incomplete from the panel.
issues.evidence: Store As naming exists only as storeAsProgram helper, split editing toggles fixed C3/C4/C5 points, morph assignment is hardcoded/clear-only, and master clock tap/dial controls are not visibly implemented.

issues.summary: Runtime displays non-finite Synth probe output.
issues.evidence: Sealed desktop capture and interactive preview status both show synth RMS as Infinity.

issues.summary: Tests pass but do not prove full canonical behavior.
issues.evidence: All required feature IDs map to one App.test.tsx; many assertions target state helpers and deterministic probes instead of the real browser UI/audio graph, and one test codifies the generated-sample deviation.
